text: 📸 Becas para el Bienestar — San Martín Texmelucan, Puebla, 13 de noviembre de 2026

🇲🇽🎨 "The presidents replicated the idea that came from outside, that 'Mexicans were lazy.' A caricature was made that, by the way, came from the United States." "And that made many Mexican women and men grow up thinking we were less. If there is something we recovered with the Governments of the Transformation, it is the dignity of the people of Mexico." "Here in Mexico our heroes came from below. Village priests led the Independence. No country in the world has a Benito Juárez García." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, inauguration of the Universidad del Deporte, Puebla, Nov 13, 2026 Sheinbaum opened the University of Sport in Puebla with Governor Alejandro Armenta and CONADE director Rommel Pacheco, and said every student there will get the Gertrudis Bocanegra scholarship. An athlete who arrives believing others are better "simply because they come from other countries" starts "with their head down," she said.

🇲🇽✊ "I think all Mexican boys and girls have talent. It's false that only some have it." "It's not true that some are better than others. It's the conditions that sometimes make one get a better grade than another." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Becas para el Bienestar, San Martín Texmelucan, Puebla, Nov 13, 2026 Critics of universal scholarships say only students with top grades should get them, Sheinbaum said. As Mexico City mayor she inherited a "Talented Children" scholarship for students averaging 9 or 10. A study of classrooms found it split students into "good" and "bad", and those left out felt less and got lower grades. After the city gave every family support, all students' grades improved. That is why the federal government now gives every public student a scholarship equally.

🇲🇽🎨 "What did education turn into? A privilege. Because only those who could pay had the privilege of going to a private school." "Why was there an exam for high school in Mexico? Do you know why? Because not enough schools were built." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Becas para el Bienestar, San Martín Texmelucan, Puebla, Nov 13, 2026 From next school year, students who finish secondary school will go straight to high school, with no admission exam. Since the Mexico City area dropped its COMIPEMS exam, 95% of students got one of their first three choices, Sheinbaum said, where before many were sent to their 15th option, sometimes 1.5 hours from home each way. She noted that the US and Europe have no high school entrance exam. In Puebla, three new technological high schools, two CBTIS expansions and 12 new Margarita Maza national high schools are under construction.

🇲🇽🌎 "In no other country in the world are all young people on scholarships." "Tomorrow we're going to leave Mexico. We're going to represent Mexico in China, at an economic forum where all the countries go. The presidents of China, the United States, Russia, Korea, Vietnam will be there. And we're going to talk, among other things, about the scholarships the government of Mexico gives so young people can study." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Becas para el Bienestar, San Martín Texmelucan, Puebla, Nov 13, 2026 Sheinbaum spoke on the eve of her trip to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in China. Every public primary student now gets school-supply and uniform support (about 9 million children), every public secondary student the Rita Cetina scholarship and every public high school student the Benito Juárez scholarship. Scholarships coordinator Julio César León said 19.5 million students are covered nationwide, 1,174,298 of them in Puebla.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>A Democratic Congress in Washington: what it means for Mexico and the T-MEC</u>

Mexico and the US traded $872 billion in goods in 2025, about $1.7 million a minute, and roughly $779 billion in the first nine months of 2026, El Economista reports. Some 16.3 million people across North America work in T-MEC supply chains. From January, Trump governs with an opposition Congress that can call hearings and question the cost of his tariffs. But Democrats like Rosa DeLauro already want tougher labor, environmental and regional-content rules, and under Biden, Washington went after policies favoring Pemex and CFE. More oversight does not mean less pressure.

🇲🇽💰 <u>Mexican workers' retirement funds gain 700 billion pesos in 2026</u>

Despite a volatile year in global markets, Mexico's retirement savings system (SAR) racked up gains of 700,384 million pesos between January and October, according to Consar. October alone added 209,427 million pesos. The money belongs to workers' Afore accounts, and Consar head Julio César Cervantes confirmed at the Amafore 2026 meeting that the year's gains have already passed 700 billion.

🇲🇽⛏️ <u>Mexico is the world's #1 silver producer. Should silver back the peso?</u>

Mexico supplies about 24% of the world's silver, more than 200 million ounces a year, ahead of China and Peru. It is also second in fluorite, fifth in lead and sixth in zinc, with copper, lithium clay and traces of uranium and thorium mapped by the Mexican Geological Service. In Contralínea, Pablo Moctezuma Barragán argues that Banxico could put part of its reserves of more than $250 billion into physical silver to back the currency and "reduce dependence on the US dollar."

🇲🇽🚌 <u>Veracruz modernizes public transit with no private operators and no debt</u>

Veracruz is rebuilding its bus systems with a public trust: fare revenue covers fuel, wages and maintenance, and the rest goes back into buying new units. "The model involves no private companies and no financing costs," Governor Rocío Nahle said, which keeps fares affordable without putting the state in debt. Four systems already run in Veracruz-Boca del Río, Coatzacoalcos-Minatitlán, Cosamaloapan and Poza Rica. The fifth, Atenas, launches November 23 in Xalapa with 60 buses to serve 900,000 riders a month.

🇲🇽❤️ <u>Sheinbaum to AMLO on his 73rd birthday: "our affection, recognition, admiration, always"</u>

Andrés Manuel López Obrador turned 73 on November 13 at his ranch in Palenque, Chiapas, far from public life since leaving office in 2024. From the National Palace, President Sheinbaum sent the country's greeting: "From here, our affection, recognition, admiration, always." Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez, Attorney General Ernestina Godoy, Welfare Secretary Leticia Ramírez, Morena leader Ariadna Montiel and Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada joined in.
